title: Statistical inverse experiments and white noise

items.title: Isonormal Gaussian white-noise inverse experiment
items.statement: Let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space, where separable means having a countable dense subset, and let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space. A real isonormal Gaussian process on $H$ is a family $Z(g)$ of real random variables with finite second moments, indexed by $g\in H$, such that $g\mapsto[Z(g)]$ is linear into $L^2(\mathbb P)$, $\mathbb E Z(g)=0$, and $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(h)]=\langle g,h\rangle_H$. It is also required that for every finite orthonormal tuple $(e_1,\ldots,e_m)$ the variables $Z(e_1),\ldots,Z(e_m)$ are independent and each has density $\varphi(t)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-t^2/2}$. For any finite list of vectors, expressing them in an orthonormal basis of their finite-dimensional span shows that their process values have the corresponding linear-image Gaussian law. Here $L^2(\mathbb P)$ identifies square-integrable random variables that agree almost surely. When $H\ne\{0\}$, all unit-vector marginals have the same law; write $N(a,\sigma^2)$ for the law of $a+\sigma Z(e)$ for any unit vector $e\in H$ and $\sigma\ge0$. Let $X$ be a set, let $\Theta\subseteq X$ be a nonempty parameter set, let $K:X\to H$ be a signal map, and let $\epsilon>0$. For $x\in\Theta$ and $g\in H$, define the observation functional $$Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g).$$ The associated statistical inverse experiment has sample space $\mathbb R^H$ with the cylinder sigma-algebra generated by the evaluation maps $y\mapsto y(g)$, and its sampling law $P_x$ is the law of the random function $g\mapsto Y_x(g)$. Each sample is indexed by test functionals on $H$; it is not asserted to be a vector in $H$ or to have a continuous path. If $H=\{0\}$, linearity forces $Z(0)=0$ and the experiment is deterministic.
items.strategy: Define the functional Gaussian experiment on the cylinder sample space using a supplied isonormal process and its mean signal; do not identify observations with H-valued samples.

references.title: Kretschmann and Werner, Maximum a posteriori testing in statistical inverse problems, §1.1, PDF pp. 1–2
Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, §1.2.2, equations (1.6)–(1.8), PDF pp. 21–22

items.title: White-noise spectral sequence representation
items.statement: Let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space with a fixed complete orthonormal basis $(u_j)$, indexed by either a finite initial segment of $\mathbb N$ or all of $\mathbb N$. Let $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g)$ be the isonormal white-noise experiment with $\epsilon>0$, and write $\mu_j=\langle Kx,u_j\rangle_H$. For every parameter $x$ and every basis index $j$, the observations $Y_x(u_j)$ are independent and have laws $N(\mu_j,\epsilon^2)$, where $N$ is the scalar normal law defined in the experiment. For $g\in H$, set $P_Ng=\sum_{j\le N}\langle g,u_j\rangle_Hu_j$, with $P_N=I$ once all vectors of a finite basis have been included. Then $$Y_x(g)=L^2(\mathbb P)\text{-}\lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{j\le N}\langle g,u_j\rangle_HY_x(u_j).$$ Thus every finite collection of observation functionals is reconstructed from the coefficient sequence in mean square; this does not assert samplewise convergence or an $H$-valued observation. If $H=L^2([0,1])$ and the basis is one of the wavelet or trigonometric bases used to define the negative Sobolev carrier $H(\delta)$, then under countable choice and for $\delta>1/2$ the same coordinate sequence is a Borel Gaussian random element in $H(\delta)$ with mean coefficients $Kx$ and noise level $\epsilon$. In infinite dimension it is not an $L^2([0,1])$-valued sample.

references.title: Kretschmann and Werner, Maximum a posteriori testing in statistical inverse problems, §1.1, PDF pp. 1–2
Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, §§1.2.2–1.2.3 and isonormal construction, PDF pp. 21–22 and 483–484
Castillo and Nickl, Nonparametric Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise, §1.2, equations (7)–(8), printed pp. 2005–2006
Ding and Mathé, Minimax rates for statistical inverse problems under general source conditions, §1, equations (1)–(3), PDF pp. 11–12

items.axiom_use: Countable choice is used only for the H(delta)-valued Borel white-noise realization, through the cited supplier lemma. The basis-coordinate and mean-square reconstruction argument uses no choice principle.

title: Statistical inverse experiments and white noise — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Two direct white-noise functionals
items.statement: Take the single-parameter experiment with $H=\mathbb R^2$, its standard inner product, parameter set $\{x\}$, mean signal $Kx=(m_1,m_2)$, and noise level $\epsilon>0$. Let $e_1=(1,0)$, $e_2=(0,1)$, and $g=ae_1+be_2$ for $a,b\in\mathbb R$. The direct observations $Y_x(e_1)$ and $Y_x(e_2)$ are independent with laws $N(m_1,\epsilon^2)$ and $N(m_2,\epsilon^2)$. In $L^2(\mathbb P)$, $Y_x(g)=aY_x(e_1)+bY_x(e_2)$, with mean $am_1+bm_2$ and variance $\epsilon^2(a^2+b^2)$; when $a=b=0$, $Y_x(g)$ is the constant zero.
items.strategy: direct example from the functional experiment definition

references.title: Kretschmann and Werner, Maximum a posteriori testing in statistical inverse problems, §1.1, PDF pp. 1–2

items.title: Gaussian coefficient sequence
items.statement: Let $H=\ell^2(\mathbb N)$ with standard basis $e_j$, take a single parameter with signal $\theta=(\theta_j)\in\ell^2(\mathbb N)$, and fix $\epsilon>0$. The coordinate statistic $Y_j=Y(e_j)=\theta_j+\epsilon Z(e_j)$ has independent coordinates with laws $N(\theta_j,\epsilon^2)$. Each finite truncation $(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N)$ therefore has the product of its $N$ scalar normal laws. The coordinate statistic takes values in $\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}$; this description does not identify the observation with an $\ell^2$-valued vector.
items.strategy: specialize the spectral sequence representation to the canonical basis of ell^2

references.title: Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, Gaussian Sequence Space Model, equation (1.8), PDF pp. 21–22

items.title: Finite truncation with its omitted white-noise tail
items.statement: Let $(u_j)$ be a fixed complete orthonormal basis, $h=Kx$ a mean signal, $g\in H$ a test vector, and $N$ a positive integer. Define $P_Ng=\sum_{j\le N}\langle g,u_j\rangle_Hu_j$ and $r_N=g-P_Ng$. Then $$Y_x(g)=\sum_{j\le N}\langle g,u_j\rangle_HY_x(u_j)+\langle h,r_N\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(r_N)$$ in $L^2(\mathbb P)$. The omitted tail has mean $\langle h,r_N\rangle_H$, variance $\epsilon^2\|r_N\|_H^2$, and is independent of the first $N$ coordinate observations. If $r_N=0$, the omitted tail vanishes.
items.strategy: decompose the test vector into its finite orthogonal projection and residual
